ColumnConstraint.doc: Per-column constraint, attached after the optional type-name. The grammar admits multiple constraints in sequence; downstream compilers fold them into table metadata.

PrimaryKey.doc: `PRIMARY KEY [ASC|DESC]`. `ascending = true` for ASC or omitted, false for DESC.

Default.doc: `DEFAULT <expr>` — value supplied when row omits the column. Expr may be any literal or parenthesized expression admitted by parse_expr.

References.doc: `REFERENCES <table> [(col [, col ...])]` — column-level FK shorthand. ON DELETE / ON UPDATE actions are deferred.

Generated.doc: `[GENERATED ALWAYS] AS (<expr>) [STORED|VIRTUAL]`. `stored = true` for STORED, false for VIRTUAL or omitted (VIRTUAL is the default).

ColumnDef.doc: One column declaration in a CREATE TABLE column list. The type-name is optional (SQLite admits typeless columns); when present it is the raw token text concatenated with spaces (e.g. `VARCHAR`, `DOUBLE PRECISION`, or `INT`). Multi-token type names admit one space-separated `Ident` sequence. Parameterized type names like `VARCHAR(30)` or `DECIMAL(10, 2)` are admitted; the integer arguments are captured in `type_params` (zero, one, or two entries). The type-name string itself does NOT include the parens; downstream consumers that don't care about width treat ColumnDef as if `type_params` was empty (CAST normalization pattern).

TableConstraint.doc: Table-level constraint, written after the column list (still inside the column-list parens, separated by comma from the last column).

ForeignKey.doc: `FOREIGN KEY (col [, col ...]) REFERENCES <table> [(col [, col ...])]`. ON DELETE / ON UPDATE actions deferred.

CreateTableStmt.doc: Parsed CREATE TABLE statement. Covers `CREATE TABLE [IF NOT EXISTS] <name> ( <col_def> [, <col_def>]* [, <table_constraint>]* ) [WITHOUT ROWID|STRICT [, WITHOUT ROWID|STRICT]]`. Schema-qualified names, temp tables, and AS-SELECT form are deferred. Parameterized type names (`VARCHAR(30)`, `DECIMAL(10,2)`) are admitted — see ColumnDef.type_params.

CreateTableParseOk.doc: Successful parse output: the CreateTableStmt plus the index of the next un-consumed token (typically `;` or `Eof`).

parse_create_table.doc: Parse a `CREATE TABLE` statement. Token at `start` must be `KwCreate`. Delegates to parse_expr for `DEFAULT`, `CHECK`, and `GENERATED ALWAYS AS` expressions. Admits parameterized type names (one or two integer args, captured in ColumnDef.type_params). Rejects deferred forms (`TEMP`, `AS SELECT`, schema-qualified names, ON DELETE/UPDATE actions) with `deferred: <construct>` ParseError.
